newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan move to privatise Big Three banks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan move to privatise Big Three banks.

text.p: A government panel has suggested that the Provincial Assembly abolish its 1989 decision not to let government stakes in the three big state-run banks fall below 51 percent, officials said on Friday.
A panel for the Taiwan Provincial Government Development Conference on Thursday agreed on the proposal, said a Finance Department official.
"The development conference will soon review the proposal, and, if approved, we plan to submit it to the Provincial Assembly for final nod," the official told Reuters by telephone.
The three banks are Chang Hwa Bank, First Bank and Hua Nan Bank.
The official said he was optimistic final approval would be given for the proposal because the development conference had been set up by both the provincial government and the provincial assembly.
"There is high recogntion in there," he said.
The reduction of the government stakes to below 51 percent will lead to the full privatisation of the three banks, analysts said.

"The news should boost Big Three share prices because once privatisation of the three is completed, their profits will increase because of higher efficiency," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.
In early Friday trade, Chang Hwa rose T$2 to T$188, First gained T$2 to T$190 and Hua Nan rose T$1 to T$146.5.
Also, Huang said, government-related funds tend to boost the share prices of the three banks to help smooth their privatisation.

In 1996, the provincial government said it would lower the state's share in each of the three banks to 51 percent first and then would negotiate with the assembly to abolish its 1989 decision not to let those stakes fall below 51 percent.
Currently, the government owns 71.35 percent of First Bank shares, 57.83 percent of Hua Nan Bank and 53.01 percent of Chang Hwa Bank.
